paragraphs: VeriPic sells a suite of digital evidence management products to law enforcement and public safety agencies. The suite runs from collecting evidence in the field through citizen-submitted uploads, organized storage, redaction and courtroom preparation. The company says agencies can use it to reduce case processing time, respond faster to FOIA and discovery requests, and organize files by case, officer or keyword.

At the center is Digital Evidence Manager (DEM), a hub where evidence from body cams, mobile uploads and witness submissions is stored, organized and accessed. Officers feed it from the field with the Evi-Pad app, which captures photo, video, audio and notes tagged by case and uploaded in real time. The public can send media through a Witness Upload web portal with no app required, and Automated Redaction blurs faces and mutes audio inside DEM. VeriPic Drive adds cloud storage for large-scale video, forensic data and long-term archives, and the product menu also lists body worn cameras, Detect-a-Fake photo authentication and a Mug Shot System. Selected files can be shared with prosecutors and other stakeholders.

VeriPic says it has partnered with law enforcement agencies for over 20 years. It positions the suite for local, county and state agencies, whether a rural department, a large metro unit or a statewide law enforcement system.
